findings: Footer change in src/take-apart-page.js is a static literal ('Blender built product model'). No new interpolation or user input reaches the template, so there is no injection surface.

/models/patch-one.glb (src/index.js:73) serves a build-time base64 constant on a fixed same-origin route with a fixed content type. It takes no user input, so there is no path traversal or SSRF risk. The client loads only '/models/patch-one.glb'.

blender/build_patch_one.py uses a seeded RNG (random.Random(4515)) for the generated microtexture. I found no network calls, subprocesses or environment reads in the added lines, so the build stays deterministic.

Low, non-blocking: the workflow downloads the Blender 4.5.15 tarball from download.blender.org over HTTPS with no checksum verification. The version is pinned and cached, but a SHA-256 check would harden the supply chain.
No secrets, deployment or merge steps are introduced. The review is written to runs/wo-gh-12/reviewer-security.output.md.
